example: *你好*，我叫小明。 — Hello, my name is Xiao Ming.
*谢谢*你的帮助。 — Thank you for your help.
*对不起*，我来晚了。 — Sorry, I'm late.
老师，*再见*！ — Goodbye, teacher!
我*是*学生。 — I am a student.
notes: Links two nouns; not used before adjectives (see 很).

example: 我*不*喝咖啡。 — I don't drink coffee.
notes: Becomes bú before a fourth tone: 不是 bú shì.

example: 我*有*一个哥哥。 — I have an older brother.
notes: Negated with 没, not 不: 没有 méiyǒu.

example: *我*很好。 — I'm fine.
notes: Add 们 for the plural: 我们 “we”.

example: *你*叫什么名字？ — What's your name?
*他*是我的朋友。 — He is my friend.
notes: 她 (she) and 它 (it) are pronounced the same.

example: 中国有很多*人*。 — China has a lot of people.
我想喝*水*。 — I'd like to drink some water.
你*吃*饭了吗？ — Have you eaten?
notes: “Have you eaten?” is an everyday greeting.

example: 他每天*喝*茶。 — He drinks tea every day.
我们*去*学校。 — We're going to school.
你什么时候*来*？ — When are you coming?

definition: to look; to watch; to read
example: 我喜欢*看*书。 — I like reading books.
你会*说*中文吗？ — Can you speak Chinese?
我*喜欢*猫。 — I like cats.

definition: to want; to think; to miss
example: 我*想*回家。 — I want to go home.
这个房间很*大*。 — This room is big.
我有一只*小*狗。 — I have a small dog.
今天天气很*好*。 — The weather is nice today.
这里人很*多*。 — There are a lot of people here.
*今天*星期一。 — Today is Monday.
*明天*见！ — See you tomorrow!
*昨天*下雨了。 — It rained yesterday.
她是我的好*朋友*。 — She's a good friend of mine.
我的*家*在北京。 — My home is in Beijing.
我每天走路去*学校*。 — I walk to school every day.
我们的*老师*很好。 — Our teacher is great.
他是大*学生*。 — He is a university student.
这本*书*很有意思。 — This book is interesting.
notes: Counted with 本 běn. Traditional: 書.

example: 这个多少*钱*？ — How much is this?
我有*一*个妹妹。 — I have a younger sister.
notes: Read yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí ge) and yì before the others; yī when counting.

example: *二*月很冷。 — February is cold.
notes: Before a measure word use 两 liǎng: 两个人 “two people”.

example: 我买了*三*本书。 — I bought three books.
我们班有*十*个学生。 — There are ten students in our class.
这是*什么*？ — What is this?
洗手间在*哪儿*？ — Where is the restroom?
notes: Southern speakers and Taiwan say 哪里 nǎlǐ. Traditional: 哪兒.

example: 我想去*中国*。 — I want to go to China.
我在学*中文*。 — I'm learning Chinese.
我*很*忙。 — I'm busy.
notes: Usually just links a subject to an adjective and adds little “very”.

example: 你好*吗*？ — How are you?
notes: Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Traditional: 嗎.

example: 这是我*的*书。 — This is my book.
我*在*家。 — I'm at home.
我*爱*我的妈妈。 — I love my mom.
他*八*岁了。 — He is eight years old.
我*爸爸*是医生。 — My dad is a doctor.
这个*杯子*是我的。 — This cup is mine.
notes: 杯 alone is a measure word: 一杯茶 “a cup of tea”.

example: 我住在*北京*。 — I live in Beijing.
我有三*本*书。 — I have three books.
notes: Used for books, notebooks and magazines.

example: “谢谢你！”“*不客气*。” — “Thank you!” “You're welcome.”
notes: Said bú kèqi: 不 becomes bú before a fourth tone. Traditional: 不客氣.

example: 这个*菜*很好吃。 — This dish is delicious.
你想喝*茶*吗？ — Would you like some tea?
我们坐*出租车*去吧。 — Let's take a taxi.
notes: You ride one with 坐 zuò. Traditional: 出租車.

example: 我晚上给你*打电话*。 — I'll call you tonight.
notes: “Call someone” is 给 + person + 打电话. Traditional: 打電話.

example: 现在三*点*。 — It's three o'clock now.
我想买一台新*电脑*。 — I want to buy a new computer.
notes: Counted with 台 tái. Traditional: 電腦.

example: 我晚上看*电视*。 — I watch TV in the evening.
我们去看*电影*吧。 — Let's go see a movie.
你想买什么*东西*？ — What do you want to buy?
notes: With full tones, dōngxī means “east and west”. Traditional: 東西.

example: 我们*都*是学生。 — We are all students.
notes: Goes before the verb and refers back to a plural subject.

example: 我在*读*一本中文书。 — I'm reading a Chinese book.
你们班有*多少*学生？ — How many students are in your class?
notes: Used for any number; 几 expects a small one.

example: 他的*儿子*五岁了。 — His son is five years old.
这家*饭馆*的菜很好吃。 — The food at this restaurant is very good.
我坐*飞机*去北京。 — I'm flying to Beijing.
请等我五*分钟*。 — Please wait five minutes for me.
认识你很*高兴*。 — Nice to meet you.
我有两*个*孩子。 — I have two children.
notes: Usually neutral tone after a number: 两个 liǎng ge. Traditional: 個.

example: 你在哪儿*工作*？ — Where do you work?
我家有一只*狗*。 — My family has a dog.
notes: Counted with 只 zhī or 条 tiáo.

example: 你的*汉语*很好。 — Your Chinese is very good.
notes: Near-synonym of 中文. Traditional: 漢語.

example: 今天几月几*号*？ — What's the date today?
我*和*我朋友去商店。 — My friend and I are going to the store.
学校*后面*有一个商店。 — There's a shop behind the school.
他明天*回*中国。 — He's going back to China tomorrow.
我*会*说一点儿汉语。 — I can speak a little Chinese.
*火车站*在哪儿？ — Where is the train station?
你家有*几*口人？ — How many people are in your family?
notes: Expects a small answer (under about ten); use 多少 for larger numbers. Traditional: 幾.

example: 你*叫*什么名字？ — What's your name?
我*九*点去学校。 — I go to school at nine.

definition: to open; to drive; to turn on
example: 请*开*门。 — Please open the door.
notes: 开车 kāichē “to drive a car”. Traditional: 開.

example: 你*看见*我的猫了吗？ — Have you seen my cat?
这个苹果三*块*钱。 — This apple costs three yuan.
notes: Spoken equivalent of 元 yuán. Traditional: 塊.

example: 我吃*了*一个苹果。 — I ate an apple.
今天很*冷*。 — It's cold today.
杯子*里*有水。 — There's water in the cup.
notes: Placed after a noun: 家里 “at home”. Traditional: 裡 (also 裏).

example: 我们*六*点吃饭。 — We eat at six.
我*妈妈*是老师。 — My mom is a teacher.
我想*买*一本书。 — I want to buy a book.
notes: Don't confuse with 卖 mài “to sell”. Traditional: 買.

example: 那只*猫*很漂亮。 — That cat is very pretty.
notes: Counted with 只 zhī. Traditional: 貓.

example: 我昨天*没*去学校。 — I didn't go to school yesterday.
notes: Negates 有 and past actions; 不 is for the present and habits. Traditional: 沒.

example: “对不起！”“*没关系*。” — “Sorry!” “That's OK.”
我想吃*米饭*。 — I'd like some rice.
我的*名字*叫小明。 — My name is Xiao Ming.
你是*哪*国人？ — Which country are you from?
notes: Often něi before a measure word in speech: 哪个 něige.

example: *那*是我的书。 — That is my book.
notes: Often nèi before a measure word in speech: 那个 nèige.

example: 我很好，你*呢*？ — I'm fine, and you?
你明天*能*来吗？ — Can you come tomorrow?
notes: For ability or permission in a situation; use 会 for learned skills.

example: 我在中国住了两*年*。 — I lived in China for two years.
notes: Takes a number directly, without 个: 一年.

example: 我*女儿*今年三岁。 — My daughter is three this year.
你的女儿真*漂亮*！ — Your daughter is so beautiful!
我每天吃一个*苹果*。 — I eat an apple every day.
一个星期有*七*天。 — There are seven days in a week.
医院在学校*前面*。 — The hospital is in front of the school.

definition: please; to invite; to treat (pay for)
example: *请*坐。 — Please sit down.
notes: 我请你 can mean “it's my treat”. Traditional: 請.

example: 今天太*热*了！ — It's too hot today!
我*认识*他。 — I know him.
notes: For people and characters; for facts use 知道 zhīdào. Traditional: 認識.

example: 我去*商店*买东西。 — I'm going to the store to buy some things.

definition: on; above; last (上个月); to go up; to get on
example: 书在桌子*上*。 — The book is on the table.
我*上午*有课。 — I have class in the morning.
今天人很*少*。 — There aren't many people today.
他是*谁*？ — Who is he?
你什么*时候*回家？ — When are you going home?
notes: 什么时候 means “when”. Traditional: 時候.

example: 我喜欢吃*水果*。 — I like eating fruit.

definition: to sleep; to go to bed
example: 我十一点*睡觉*。 — I go to bed at eleven.
notes: 觉 is jiào here, not jué. Traditional: 睡覺.

example: 我家有*四*口人。 — There are four people in my family.
你今年几*岁*？ — How old are you this year?
notes: 几岁 is for children; ask adults 多大. Traditional: 歲.

example: *她*是我妹妹。 — She is my younger sister.
这个*太*贵了。 — This is too expensive.
notes: Usually in the pattern 太…了.

example: 明天*天气*怎么样？ — What's the weather like tomorrow?
我喜欢*听*音乐。 — I like listening to music.
他是我的*同学*。 — He's my classmate.
*喂*，你好！ — Hello? (on the phone)
notes: Said wéi on the phone; wèi is a blunt “hey!”.

example: *我们*一起去吧。 — Let's go together.
我们*五*个人一起去。 — The five of us are going together.

definition: below; next (下个月); to go down; to get off
example: 你在哪儿*下*车？ — Where are you getting off?
我们*下午*去看电影。 — We're going to see a movie this afternoon.
外面在*下雨*。 — It's raining outside.
王*先生*是我的老师。 — Mr. Wang is my teacher.
notes: Comes after the surname: 王先生.

example: *现在*几点？ — What time is it now?
李*小姐*是医生。 — Miss Li is a doctor.
我买了一*些*水果。 — I bought some fruit.
你会*写*汉字吗？ — Can you write Chinese characters?
我下个*星期*去北京。 — I'm going to Beijing next week.
notes: Days: 星期一 Monday … 星期六 Saturday, 星期天 Sunday.

example: 我在大学*学习*汉语。 — I study Chinese at university.
这件*衣服*很漂亮。 — This piece of clothing is pretty.
我想当*医生*。 — I want to become a doctor.
他在*医院*工作。 — He works at a hospital.
这里有一把*椅子*。 — There's a chair here.
我在中国住了三个*月*。 — I lived in China for three months.
notes: 三个月 is “three months”; 三月 is “March”.

example: 去火车站*怎么*走？ — How do I get to the train station?
你的新工作*怎么样*？ — How's your new job?
*这*是我的朋友。 — This is my friend.
notes: Often zhèi before a measure word in speech: 这个 zhèige. Traditional: 這.

example: 我们*中午*在饭馆吃饭。 — We're having lunch at a restaurant.
你*住*在哪儿？ — Where do you live?
*桌子*上有一个杯子。 — There's a cup on the table.
这个*字*怎么读？ — How do you read this character?
我们*坐*火车去吧。 — Let's go by train.
notes: Used for riding vehicles: 坐飞机, 坐出租车.

example: 你在*做*什么？ — What are you doing?
